solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Call with little flower

definitions.meaning: a summons, as in being at someone's ... and call
a small stream; in crosswords a flower is something that flows, so a little one is a brook

explanation.surface: A request to someone, accompanied by a tiny bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is read as 'something that flows', a river, not a bloom. A beck is a northern English word for a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a summoning gesture, and a small brook in northern English dialect.

clue.text: Physical injury? Get joint loosening initially in watery mixture

indicators.note: the joint and the first letter sit inside the watery mixture

parts.note: a wash is a thin liquid mixture, such as pig swill or a colour wash
the hip is a joint of the body

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word loosening is taken

explanation.surface: Advice on easing a stiff joint by soaking it in some liquid preparation.
explanation.definitionFit: The neck injury from a sudden jolt, as in a car crash, is a common physical injury.

clue.text: Little son, dull-sounding — and not tall and handsome

parts.note: son shortened to its abbreviation S
tubby describes a dull, flat sound like a tub being struck

explanation.surface: A description of a small boy with a flat voice who is far from a dashing figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Short and thickset, the reverse of a tall and handsome build.

clue.text: Christian Union chaps outside a college making new convert?

indicators.note: the union and the chaps go round the outside of the college piece

parts.note: CU, the usual abbreviation for a student Christian Union
a tech is a technical college
men

explanation.surface: A student Christian group gathers around a college hoping to make a convert.
explanation.definitionFit: In the early Church a person receiving instruction before baptism was a newcomer to the faith.

clue.text: Wood — in retrospect, master conductor

parts.note: beech is a type of wood

indicators.note: looking back, so the letters for master are read backwards

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: Looking back on a great orchestral conductor, perhaps Sir Henry Wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Wood was a famous British conductor, so 'Wood' wants to be a conductor; it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas Beecham was a celebrated English orchestral conductor, so this is an example.

clue.text: Bishop of pale complexion, a respected white man once?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
wan means pale

explanation.surface: A cleric with a pallid face, regarded as a respected European in colonial times.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swahili term of respect, master or sir, used in colonial East Africa for a European man.

clue.text: Type of plant in old economy, not new

indicators.note: the letters are made new, arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A plant thriving in a traditional economy rather than a modern one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal on OLD ECONOMY NOT, all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant with a single seed leaf, such as grasses and lilies, is a botanical category.

clue.text: Walk a mile in journey? Not I

indicators.note: the a and the mile go inside what is left of the journey
says the letter I is left out of the journey word

parts.note: a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: Someone declining to walk a mile on an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or trek a long distance, a close synonym.

clue.text: Vegetable row with more fertiliser in?

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A row of vegetables in a garden bed that has been well manured.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat is used to enrich soil, so ground containing more of it is richer in that fertiliser.

clue.text: Airborne group stop operating

parts.note: a pack is a group, as of wolves or cubs
up in the air

explanation.surface: A unit of paratroopers ceasing operations.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that breaks down or a person who quits is said to give up working, an idiom.

clue.text: VIP and old sweetheart making you peer

parts.note: a nob is a person of high social standing
leman is an archaic word for a lover

explanation.surface: An important person and a former flame prompting you to look closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' looks like a verb meaning to look; it is the noun, a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled aristocrat such as a duke or earl is a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Male with an attempt to limit one cunning woman wearing the trousers in this?

definitions.text: woman wearing the trousers in this?

indicators.note: the attempt encloses, so limits, the one and the cunning

parts.note: a try is an attempt
I is the Roman numeral one
arch means slyly mischievous

explanation.surface: A man tries to curb a crafty woman who is the dominant partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A society or household ruled by women is one where a woman is in charge, idiomatically wears the trousers.

clue.text: Person in church maybe pinching stuff from roof? Number one villain

indicators.note: holding tight around, so the bell-ringer goes round the roof material

parts.note: a bell-ringer works in a church tower
lead is a roofing material, often stolen from churches

explanation.surface: A churchgoer caught stealing roofing metal, the chief culprit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like stealing, which suits lead theft; it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of a gang of wrongdoers is its chief, the top villain.

clue.text: One requiring no effort to succeed

definitions.text: One requiring no effort to succeed

parts.words: One requiring no effort to succeed
parts.note: to succeed here means to inherit a title or estate, which needs no work beyond being next in line

explanation.definitionFit: A person next in line to inherit simply takes over by birth or bequest, without earning it.

clue.text: Glum mother and son suffering in a period of unrest in the Sixties

definitions.text: a period of unrest in the Sixties

indicators.note: the letters are in a distressed, disordered state

explanation.surface: A miserable mother and her son going through hard times during a turbulent decade.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the summer of 1967, when race riots broke out across American cities.

clue.text: Making escape from police criminal is brilliant

parts.note: to lam is to flee, as in being on the lam
bent is slang for corrupt or criminal

explanation.surface: A criminal who gets away from the police is thought very clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Softly glowing or flickering, or brilliantly witty, as in lambent humour.

clue.text: Like some deliveries coming by hand in the pit?

definitions.text: Like some deliveries coming by hand
definitions.meaning: in cricket a ball bowled with the hand below the shoulder
located beneath the arm, in the armpit

explanation.surface: Packages handed over by a miner working down the pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: bowled with the hand kept low, and positioned below the shoulder.

clue.text: Little woman — Liberal or Radical?

parts.note: Amy March is one of the sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A question about a small woman's politics: moderate or extreme?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' looks political; it is the chemistry sense, a group of atoms.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a radical is a group of atoms acting as a unit, and this pentyl group is one.

clue.text: Fella dines extravagantly — no sign of this?

indicators.note: wildly and lavishly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A man eating lavishly shows no restraint at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from pleasures is exactly what is missing when someone feasts lavishly.

clue.text: Lustrous metal state imports

indicators.note: brings in, so the metal goes inside the word for state

parts.note: to say is to state
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A shiny metal that a country brings in from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a nation; it is the verb, to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a smooth glossy sheen like silk fabric, hence shining.

clue.text: Number one man's here? One of two such in USA

definitions.meaning: a playful reading: the possessive of the first man, as if asking whose place this is

definitions.text: One of two such in USA
definitions.meaning: two US presidents, John and John Quincy, bore this surname

explanation.surface: A question about where the top man is, comparing two in America.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and his son John Quincy Adams were both US presidents, the two of that surname.

clue.text: Occupied like camp able to accommodate a number

indicators.note: having room for, so the a and number go inside

parts.note: a camp is tented, covered with tents
N is the mathematical symbol for a number

explanation.surface: A campsite big enough to hold a certain number of people is full.
explanation.definitionFit: A property that has tenants living in it is lived in, so filled.

clue.text: Composer making hit disc for us to hear?

parts.note: to ram is to hit forcefully

indicators.note: signals a word spoken that sounds like a written one

parts.note: a disc is a round shape like the letter O

explanation.surface: A composer producing a hit record for listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disc' looks like a record; it is the round shape O, and EAU, French for water, is pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Philippe Rameau was a French baroque composer, an example.

clue.text: Illness gripping one? This would give body protection

indicators.note: holding tight around, so the illness surrounds the one

parts.note: mal is French for illness, as in mal de mer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sickness taking hold of someone, who needs protecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain armour of interlinked rings protected the knight's body in battle.

clue.text: Old aristocrat in Ghent wandering around

indicators.note: the letters roam about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A noble of former times roaming the streets of a Belgian city.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Saxon England this was a man holding land from the king, a nobleman of that era.

clue.text: Worms in nests before being captured

indicators.note: the word for before is held inside the nests

parts.note: a nid or nide is a pheasant's nest
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Worms found in birds' nests just before they are caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine bristle worms are named after these sea nymphs; it is a zoological name for ragworms.
